title: Software for Independent Martial Arts Instructors (2026)
description: Teach without your own gym? 10 tools compared for instructors: $0 plans, fees at 12 vs 30 students, private lessons, multiple venues and waivers.
h1: Software for independent martial arts instructors
body:
Plenty of martial arts instructors teach without a gym of their own: classes on rented mats, at a YMCA or community center, in a school gym after hours, or private lessons in a client's garage. You don't need door access, a front-desk kiosk or a 300-student pricing tier. You need a way for students to sign up and sign a waiver, collect monthly or per-class payments, book private lessons, and maybe run classes at more than one venue, all without a big monthly fee eating a small roster.

This guide compares what ten vendors publish on exactly those points. We checked each vendor's own pricing and feature pages on November 25, 2026. We haven't used these tools ourselves and we don't publish ratings. Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. Prices are in US dollars. If you're opening your own school instead, see best software for a new dojo; if you just want the lowest sticker price, see free and low-cost martial arts software.

What an instructor without a gym actually needs

  • Small-roster pricing. A $0 plan, or a low flat fee at 10 to 30 students. Watch for percentage fees, which grow with your income.
  • Online signup with a waiver and payment. You may not have a front desk, so the student should be able to join from a link.
  • Private lesson booking. 1:1 sessions with your availability and reminders.
  • More than one venue. If you teach Tuesdays at one place and Saturdays at another, check whether the plan allows more than one location.
  • Belt or rank tracking if you grade students. The general booking tools (Arketa, Vagaro) aren't built for this.
  • Easy exit. Venue arrangements change; a month-to-month plan matters more than features.

What it costs: 12 students vs 30 students

Say each student pays $100 a month by card. With 12 students that's $1,200 a month and 12 card payments; with 30 students it's $3,000 and 30 payments. Stripe's standard US rate is 2.9% + 30¢ per domestic card payment (stripe.com/pricing, checked 2026-11-25), so Stripe takes $38.40 a month at 12 students and $96 at 30.

Our arithmetic from the published prices above. Taxes, ACH, cash payments, add-ons and chargebacks are left out. Paying by ACH instead of card lowers the percentage on several tools; see payment processing fees explained.

The ranking flips as you grow. At 12 students the $0 plans with a percentage fee (MatPilot Free, PushPress Free) cost about the same as each other and well under the flat-fee martial arts tools (about $98 to $116 with Stripe or Basys). By 30 students MatPilot Free, PushPress Free and MatGoat Professional land in the same range (about $156 to $159), and a flat plan with no platform fee starts to make sense as your roster keeps growing. Recess is the only tool here where the instructor pays nothing and the families pay the fee instead; whether that suits your students is your call.

Teaching at more than one venue

If you run classes in two places, check the location rules before you build your schedule. Martialytics lists "Unlimited locations" on every plan, Recess says $0 "at any number of locations", and MatPilot lists "more than one site" under staff and locations. PushPress prices each location separately, but its Free plan is $0 per location. Arketa's Individual plan is limited to 1 location, so a second venue means talking to Arketa about a Studio plan (price by quote). Kicksite offers multi-location accounts but doesn't publish the price. See martial arts software for multiple locations for how extra-location fees work on larger tools.

Private lessons

Private lessons are a big share of income for many independent instructors. MatPilot (one-on-one sessions with buffers and reminders), PushPress (appointments), Recess (appointments), RhinoFit (appointment scheduling on all plans), Arketa Individual (privates and semi-privates, Google Calendar sync) and Vagaro (appointment booking) all publish this. MatGoat, MAAT, Kicksite and Martialytics don't state appointment booking on the pricing pages we checked, so ask during the trial if you sell privates.

Signup links and waivers

MatPilot describes "one link: plan, waiver and payment before the first class". RhinoFit lists RhinoSign digital waivers on every plan, including Start Up. Kicksite lists digital waivers and agreements sent by email or text. For the others, waiver features aren't stated on the pages we checked.

How to choose

  • Under about 20 students and you grade belts: MatPilot Free, PushPress Free (belt tracking is Pro only), RhinoFit Start Up, or Recess if your families accept a checkout fee.
  • Mostly private lessons, no belt system: a general booking tool like Arketa Individual or Vagaro can be enough; note Arketa's 3% fee and 1-location limit.
  • Several venues: Martialytics, Recess or MatPilot publish multi-location support at no listed extra cost.
  • Growing past 30 students: compare flat plans (MatGoat Professional $60, Martialytics $69, MatPilot Pro $79 + 0.49%) against percentage fees. Our cheap martial arts software page and the martial arts software hub cover more options.

faq: What is the cheapest software for a martial arts instructor without a gym?

Recess charges the instructor $0 a month; members pay a service fee of about 5% at checkout. MatPilot Free is $0 a month plus a 2% platform fee and Stripe's fee, PushPress Free is $0 with 4.99% + $0.30 per card payment, and RhinoFit Start Up is $0 for 20 or fewer active users and $2,500 or less in monthly payments in the US and Canada (vendor pricing pages, checked 2026-11-25).
Can I book private martial arts lessons with these tools?

MatPilot, PushPress, Recess, RhinoFit, Arketa (Individual plan) and Vagaro publish appointment or private-session booking. MatGoat, MAAT, Kicksite and Martialytics don't state it on the pricing pages we checked on 2026-11-25, so ask the vendor.
I teach at two different venues. Which software supports that?

Martialytics lists unlimited locations on every plan, Recess says $0 at any number of locations, and MatPilot lists more than one site. PushPress prices per location (Free is $0 per location). Arketa's Individual plan allows 1 location (pricing pages, checked 2026-11-25).
Do I need martial arts software or will a general booking app work?

General tools like Arketa Individual ($49/mo billed annually plus a 3% fee) and Vagaro ($30/mo for one calendar) handle classes and private bookings, but they don't publish belt or rank tracking. Martial arts tools such as MatPilot, Recess, RhinoFit, MatGoat, MAAT, Kicksite and Martialytics include belt tracking.
